prompt.es: Parafrasea el párrafo en 60–80 palabras: dos verbos de cita y una nominalización.

answer.text: According to the study, the new bike lanes have led to a rapid growth in cycling and a reduction in car traffic. The lead researcher argues that the investment has already paid for itself, and she points out that shop sales along the lanes have risen. Critics claim, however, that the results for small shops are unreliable. She acknowledges this limitation and suggests repeating the survey with a larger sample.
accepted: According to the study, the new bike lanes have led to a rapid growth in cycling and a reduction in car traffic. The lead researcher argues that the investment has already paid for itself, and she points out that shop sales along the lanes have risen. Critics claim, however, that the results for small shops are unreliable. She acknowledges this limitation and suggests repeating the survey with a larger sample.

The study shows a rise in cycling and a decrease in traffic after the city built bike lanes. The researcher maintains that the project has paid for itself, and she notes that shops along the lanes sell more. Some critics claim that the information about small businesses is incomplete, and she acknowledges that a larger survey is needed next year.

feedback.es: Una buena paráfrasis atribuye con dos verbos distintos, condensa con una nominalización y conserva las ideas clave con otras palabras.

origin.text: Five years ago, the city council decided to build more than one hundred kilometres of protected bike lanes. At first, many residents were against the plan. Shop owners were especially worried, because they believed that fewer parking places would mean fewer customers. However, the figures published this spring tell a different story. The number of people who cycle to work has risen from three per cent to eleven per cent, and car traffic in the centre has fallen by nine per cent. Air quality has also improved, and the noise in the main streets has decreased. Several schools have reported that more pupils now come to class by bicycle. The researcher who led the study argues that the investment has already paid for itself, because the city now spends less on road repairs and on health care. She points out that sales in the shops along the new lanes have grown by six per cent. Nevertheless, some critics claim that the results for small shops are unreliable, since only forty businesses answered the survey. The researcher acknowledges this limitation, and she suggests that the council should repeat the survey next year with a larger sample.
